comments.author: santastabber
comments.text:
A second run independently reproduced the same delay, with the core runtime unchanged.

All identifiers below are symbolic; times are relative to the child enqueue. No customer data, private URLs, actual workflow/execution IDs, inputs or result bodies are included.

| Event | Relative time |
|---|---:|
| Calling worker A enqueues child | +0.000 s |
| Worker B starts child | +0.012 s |
| Worker B reports completion | +1.655 s |
| Main receives completion | +1.657 s |
| Calling worker A logs `ended without a completion event, resolving the wait from the DB` | +60.008 s |

The persisted child execution took **1.623 s**, while the native Agent workflow tool call took **60.083 s**. Its successful result was only **243 characters**.

Same-run MCP calls returned promptly (for example, CIPP tenant listing **0.822 s**, Hudu company listing **0.387 s**, and Jitbit ticket listing **1.503 s**). These use the MCP request/response path rather than the native Agent workflow tool's caller-worker completion wait. This comparison is consistent with the missing worker outcome listeners described above.

This adds a second observed occurrence to the original timing evidence. The proposed core patch remains **undeployed**.

Additional route comparison: after exposing the **same, unchanged lookup subworkflow** through an authenticated MCP server, a built-in native Agent test called the MCP version in **1.761 s**. It used the same name-query input and returned the same `no_match` / `name_search` outcome. The test made exactly one tool call. No n8n core patch was deployed. This further isolates the long delay to the native workflow-tool dispatch/completion path rather than the lookup's database/model processing.

comments.author: leomattos7
comments.text: Hi! I'd like to pick this up. I checked current `master`: `registerWorkerListeners()` still handles only `abort-job`, so a worker that enqueued a child job only learns the outcome from the 60s DB recheck. I have a fix ready that shares the outcome handling between the main/webhook and worker listeners, with unit tests that fail on `master`. Happy to open the PR if the team is fine with a community fix. @santastabber thanks for the analysis and the patch, I'll credit you in the PR.

comments.author: donleco2474
comments.text: That ~60-second delay on distributed worker nodes stems from ScalingService.registerWorkerListeners() omitting child completion and failure event bindings in JobOutcomeTracker, which forces the caller to time out and poll the database instead of catching the pub/sub notification instantly. Patching the worker listener registration to forward child outcome events directly through Redis pub/sub eliminates the polling fallback. If you are tracking down the exact event emitter bindings in your build, let me know and I can share the specific hook adjustments right here.
